description.value: The study examined whether simple multiplication processing differs between bilingual adults' language of learning and their other language, using behavioral measures and fMRI, with exploratory analyses of problem size, vocabulary fluency, and Bayesian language effects.

design.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults were recruited; six were excluded, leaving 29 participants. Participants completed two localizer tasks and a single-digit multiplication verification task during one experimental session. The verbal and multiplication tasks were administered in English and Spanish, with language order alternated across participants. fMRI activation was analyzed within functionally constrained anatomical ROIs and at the whole-brain level.

description.value: Test 14: Picture Vocabulary and Test 15: Oral Comprehension were used to determine English language proficiency.
Equivalent Spanish versions of the language proficiency tests were administered, including Picture Vocabulary, Oral Comprehension, and Vocabulario Sobre Dibujos.
Test 8: Incomplete Words was used to assess phonological awareness in English.
Aged-normalized classifications were obtained from raw assessment scores in each language and compared across parallel subtests.

name.value: Math Fluency: Multiplication subtest of the Wechsler Individual Achievement Test (WIAT)

description.value: Participants answered as many single-digit multiplication problems as possible in 60 seconds.
Handedness was assessed using the Edinburgh Inventory; scores ranged from 0.35 to 1.00.
A measure of working memory was collected for use outside the scope of the current research questions.

clinical_characteristics.value: All participants reported Spanish as their native language (L1), with 8 participants also reporting English as a simultaneous native language. Eleven individuals learned multiplication in Spanish, and 18 reported learning multiplication in English. All participants reported using English as their current preferred math language, with 2 individuals additionally reporting to prefer Spanish depending on the context.

medication_status.value: not taking medication that affected their cognition at the time of testing; one participant was excluded due to taking psychoactive medications at the time of testing

task_description.value: Participants heard two spoken number words, followed by a visual Arabic digit, and determined whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers.

instructions.value: Participants determined whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers. They used their index finger if the proposed solution was true and their middle finger if the proposed solution was false.

stimuli.value: Two spoken number words followed by a visual Arabic digit; participants did not see any written words. Thirty-six single-digit multiplication problems and 12 control trials were presented per run.

stimuli.value: Black-and-white line drawings followed by spoken words in English or Spanish; 40 experimental trials and 13 control trials were presented per run.

description.value: Before functional image acquisition, a high-resolution T1-weighted 3D structural image was acquired for each participant with TR = 1,900 ms, TE = 2.43 ms, matrix size = 256 x 256, field of view = 256 mm, slice thickness = 1 mm, and number of slices = 192.

Functional images were realigned, an anatomical brain mask was created from segmentation products, functional images were co-registered to the skull-stripped anatomical image, normalized to the standard T1 Montreal Neurological Institute template, smoothed with a 6 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel, and motion outlier volumes were identified and repaired by interpolation.

steps.value: all functional images were realigned to their mean functional image across runs
an anatomical brain mask was created by combining grey matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid segmentation products
the mean functional image and all functional images were co-registered to the skull-stripped anatomical image
all functional images were normalized to the standard T1 Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothing was applied with a 6 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel
outlier volumes were identified using Art-Repair and repaired by interpolation between the nearest non-outlier volumes
six motion parameters estimated during realignment were entered in first-level modeling and repaired volumes were deweighted

model_settings.value: Activation was modeled as epochs with onsets time-locked to the presentation of the first stimulus in each trial. All proposed solutions and all participants’ responses were included in the model. The time series data were high-pass filtered at 1/128 Hz, and serial correlations were corrected using an autoregressive AR model. Six motion parameters were entered as regressors and repaired volumes were deweighted.
Language, Problem size, and Correctness were modeled with Subjects as a random effect; Satterthwaite’s method was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom for F statistics.

estimator.value: generalized linear model from the lme4 package in R

model_settings.value: Brain data were modeled based on Problem Size, Language, and the additive effect with and without the interaction between the two. The Watanabe information criteria comparison (WAIC) was used to determine which model best fit the data, and posterior summaries provided Bayesian p-values.

estimator.value: Watanabe information criteria comparison (WAIC) and posterior summaries

model_settings.value: LA+ vocabulary fluency was entered as a covariate of no interest and LA- vocabulary fluency as the independent variable. Separate models were conducted for accuracy, response time, and brain activation.
